problems: xiongnu and southern-xiongnu share Q188836 but are different states: the xiongnu dossier keeps cliopatria_names ['Xiongnu'] and records the 48 CE secession as a split; the southern-xiongnu dossier (another ia-01 part) must list xiongnu as predecessor and carry the 50 CE Han vassalage, and Cliopatria's second Han-Xiongnu alliance row (30..105) belongs to it.

Cliopatria's Xiongnu shapes 106..153 (Ili/Kazakh steppe) are the Yueban, a different polity: marked wrong and redrawn as the Dzungaria-Barkol remnant; the Xiongnu end year is set to 151 (the Ikh Bayan page would end the state in 93).
Cliopatria's Yuezhi homeland shapes (404-171 BCE) lie west of Dunhuang into Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan while the pages put the Yuezhi in the Hexi Corridor and eastern Xinjiang: all four marked adjust.
Yuezhi -> Kushan Empire (kushan-empire, sa-02) is written as a successor state; the continuity is strong enough that the colour agent may want one hue for both.

WebFetch of the Scythians article returns text that stops in the late 5th century BCE; offset reads gave nothing more, so the decline rests on four other pages. Northern_Xiongnu and Southern_Xiongnu are redirects to Xiongnu (no separate articles). Han%E2%80%93Xiongnu_War failed but Han-Xiongnu_War loaded; List_of_chanyus failed and the Chanyu article supplied the ruler list.
sources_total counts the 22 distinct URLs opened across the four dossiers (20 articles plus the two redirects); the per-dossier sources sum to 30 because pages are shared.
The 1-page validator warnings that remain are counterpart slugs without dossiers (sakas, sarmatians); zhizhi-xiongnu now exists.
